chose: The cast comes in through the template's shape (`cast: "cast-v1"`), as the brand's motion and theme do, so a version already pinned keeps the flat icons and a published essay's version never redraws. The Rust essay's version 6 and the interview essay's version 3 name it; each draws everything the version before it does. Rust Rounds writes version 6 where it wrote 5 (an essay with an opening), and the interview week writes 3 where it wrote 2. This moves C270 for an essay with an opening: it could still be drawn at the older version, but takes the cast's, so home's render image refuses it (VS1) until the owner rebuilds that image from a some-ui with this change. An essay with no opening still takes the lowest version that draws it, as C270 chose, and keeps the flat icons. A cards essay's spoken card, which has no format of its own, takes its cast from its series as it takes its theme (C816): cheat-sheet v3 names cast-v1, so a spoken card draws the same birds and mochi through the same bubble.
options: an opt-in shape field, new versions only (chosen)
draw the cast in every version: simpler, but an essay already published would redraw differently from what was released
always write the newest version: gives every essay the cast, but moves C270 for every essay, those with no opening too, so each waits on a rebuilt render image
gray: Which essays show the characters, and when, is something the owner sees; no check settled it. The costs: home's render image must be rebuilt before the next essay with an opening renders, the same step every template version has asked for; and an essay with no opening keeps the flat icons until its producer writes a cast version.
undo: Drop `cast` from the essay versions' shapes and the schema, delete `rust-essay/v6.json`, and set ESSAY_VERSION back to 5 and INTERVIEW_ESSAY_VERSION to 2; essays written at 6 or 3 are then refused (VS1).
